subroutines.name: plot_sprite
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite
subroutines.description: Copy sprite sprite_number to the screen with its top-left corner at byte column plot_x, pixel row plot_y. The sprite tables give the address of its data and its size; the data is stored row by row, sprite_width bytes to a row, and is written over the screen contents without masking. The screen is laid out like MODE 2 with 640-byte character rows from &3000, so successive bytes of a sprite row are 8 bytes apart, and each pixel row starts one byte below the last, or 640-7 bytes on when it crosses into the next character row.

subroutines.name: screen_address
subroutines.title: Calculate a screen address
subroutines.description: Set screen_ptr to the screen address of byte column plot_x on pixel row plot_y: &3000 + 640 x (plot_y DIV 8) + (plot_y MOD 8) + 8 x plot_x. The multiplication by 640 is done with a table inside MOS 1.20 (mos_row_offsets), so this only works with that MOS.

subroutines.name: wrch_handler
subroutines.title: WRCHV handler: print letters and digits in the game font
subroutines.description: Installed on WRCHV while the game runs. A letter (either case) or a digit is printed in the game's own font: its eight-byte glyph is copied over the definition of character 128 (user_char_128) and character 128 is printed instead. Every other character is printed unchanged. Both paths finish in the MOS 1.20 OSWRCH routine at mos_oswrch_default, jumped to directly rather than through the WRCHV value saved at start-up.

banners.name: font_letters
banners.title: Font: letters A-Z
banners.description: Eight bytes per letter, copied into the definition of character 128 by the WRCHV handler.

banners.name: font_digits
banners.title: Font: digits 0-9
banners.description: Eight bytes per digit, copied into the definition of character 128 by the WRCHV handler.

memory_map.name: plot_x
memory_map.description: Sprite position: screen byte column, 0-79 (two MODE 2 pixels per byte). Also used as a scratch byte and pointer low byte by other routines.

memory_map.name: plot_y
memory_map.description: Sprite position: pixel row from the top of the screen. Also used as a pointer high byte by other routines.

memory_map.name: sprite_width
memory_map.description: Width of the sprite being plotted, in screen bytes.

memory_map.name: sprite_height
memory_map.description: Height of the sprite being plotted, in pixel rows.

memory_map.name: screen_ptr
memory_map.description: Screen address being written, low byte.

memory_map.name: screen_ptr_hi
memory_map.description: Screen address being written, high byte.

memory_map.name: row_start_ptr
memory_map.description: Screen address of the first byte of the sprite row being plotted, low byte.

memory_map.name: row_start_ptr_hi
memory_map.description: Screen address of the first byte of the sprite row being plotted, high byte.

memory_map.name: sprite_data_ptr
memory_map.description: Address of the next sprite data byte to plot, low byte.

memory_map.name: sprite_data_ptr_hi
memory_map.description: Address of the next sprite data byte to plot, high byte.

memory_map.name: sprite_number
memory_map.description: Sprite to plot: an index into the sprite tables at sprite_addr_lo, sprite_addr_hi, sprite_widths and sprite_heights.

memory_map.name: os_vsync_counter
memory_map.description: MOS 1.20 counter decremented on every vertical sync interrupt. The game sets it and waits for it to run out to pace itself.

memory_map.name: mos_row_offsets
memory_map.description: MOS 1.20 table of screen row offsets for 640-byte rows (row x 640, high byte then low byte, one pair per character row). Read directly by screen_address; it is not part of any documented interface.

memory_map.name: mos_oswrch_default
memory_map.description: MOS 1.20 default OSWRCH routine, WRCHV's initial value. The WRCHV handler jumps here directly instead of through the saved vector.
